result.result:
The budget tracker is built and covers all 11 requirements. The final run was clean: 20 of 20 logic tests passed, both browser walkthroughs (1280px and 375px) passed, and type-checking, lint and the production build had no errors. Start it with `npm run dev` and open http://localhost:5214.

**How it works:**
- **Money:** amounts are stored as whole cents and only turned into decimals for display and the CSV file. Adding 0.1 and 0.2 shows **0.30**.
- **Where the logic lives:** `src/lib/money.ts` and `src/lib/budget.ts` hold the calculations: totals, chart slices, budgets, filters, validation, CSV and saving. The screens are in `src/App.tsx` and `src/components/`.
- **Filters:** they narrow only the transaction list. The totals, chart and budgets always show the whole month, and the list says "Showing X of Y" when a filter is on.
- **Budgets:** each category's budget is a monthly amount that applies to every month. Over budget, the bar turns red and the text says "over by X", so it doesn't rely on colour alone.
- **CSV:** the file is named `budget-YYYY-MM.csv`. Commas and quotes in notes are escaped, and a note starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` gets a leading `'` so a spreadsheet won't run it as a formula.
- **Things I added that you didn't ask for:**
  - You can delete your own categories; their transactions move to Other.
  - Changing a transaction's date to another month moves it there, and a message tells you which month.
  - Data stays in sync across open tabs.
  - A warning appears if the browser refuses to save.
  - Damaged saved data falls back to the defaults instead of crashing the page.
- **Changes to the project setup:** I added `vitest` as a dev dependency, plus `npm test` and `npm run test:e2e` scripts. Nothing is committed.

**What I tested and how**
- **Logic tests** (`src/lib/budget.test.ts`, 20 tests, `npm test`):
  - Reading amounts like `12,50`, `1,234.56` and `.5`, and rejecting 0, negatives, text, `1e3` and more than 2 decimals.
  - 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30, number formatting, and date checks including Feb 30 and leap years.
  - Moving between months across a year end, and the default date for a new transaction.
  - Picking the month's transactions, totals, chart slices, and budgets including "exactly on budget is not over".
  - All three filters and the search, the form's error messages, and duplicate category names.
  - CSV escaping and formula protection, and loading saved data that is damaged or out of date.
- **Browser tests** (`e2e/app.spec.ts`, `npx playwright test`, real Chrome), running the same full walkthrough at 1280px and 375px:
  - The validation messages appear (empty amount, 0, -4, "abc", missing date) and nothing gets saved.
  - Adding, editing, cancelling an edit, and deleting.
  - Totals, including 0.1 + 0.2 shown as 0.30.
  - The chart shows the right slices, ignores income, and the hover readout works.
  - Budgets turn red when over and the progress value is correct; a budget of 0 is rejected.
  - A custom category with a chosen colour shows up in the chart.
  - The category, type and note filters, plus "Clear filters".
  - The downloaded CSV's contents are checked line by line.
  - Next, previous and Today in the month switcher, and an empty month showing zeros.
  - Moving a transaction to another month, and everything still being there after a reload.
  - No sideways scrolling and no console errors.
- **Screenshots I looked at myself** (in `shots/`): from them I fixed category names disappearing from the chart legend at desktop width, small shares showing as "0.0%" (now "<0.1%"), and the mobile header wrapping awkwardly. On mobile the chart now sits above the categories panel. I re-ran everything after these fixes.

There's now a "Clear filters" button next to the filters, and income shows in teal. The 20 logic tests and both browser walkthroughs (1280px and 375px) pass, and type-checking and lint are clean.

- **Clear filters button:** it sits at the end of the filter row on desktop. On mobile it shares a row with the search box, under the two dropdowns. It's greyed out until a filter is active, and one click resets the category, type and search together.
- **Removed:** the "Clear filters" link that used to appear only in the "No transactions match" message. Two buttons with the same name would have been redundant.
- **Teal income:** the income total and the "+" amounts in the transaction list now use Tailwind's `teal-700`.
- **Not changed:** the "Transaction added" message is still green. It's a confirmation message, not an income figure, so I left it alone. Say if you want it teal too.

All changes are in `src/App.tsx`, plus new checks in `e2e/app.spec.ts`. Nothing is committed.

**What I checked**
- **Logic tests** (`npm test`): all 20 pass, unchanged.
- **Browser tests** (`npx playwright test`, real Chrome, at 1280px and 375px): the full walkthrough from last time still passes, plus new checks that:
  - The button is disabled with no filters and enabled once one is set.
  - With all three filters set ("Showing 1 of 4"), one click clears the category, type and search, and all 4 rows come back.
  - The button is on the same line as the search box, to its right, at both widths.
  - The browser's computed colour of the income total and of the Salary row's amount is teal-700.
  - There is no sideways scrolling and no console errors.
- **Screenshots I looked at** (`shots/desktop-filters-active.png`, `shots/mobile-filters-active.png`, `shots/mobile-final.png`):
  - The button lines up neatly at both sizes and its disabled state looks right.
  - The teal is clearly different from the green "Transaction added" message.
  - Nothing overflows on mobile.

Recurring transactions work as you specified. In the final run all 47 logic tests passed, all 4 browser walkthroughs passed (the original requirements plus the new recurring ones, each at 1280px and 375px), and type-checking, lint and the build were clean.

**How it behaves**
- **Marking:** the add and edit forms have a "Repeat monthly" checkbox. Repeating transactions get a "↻ Monthly" tag in the list.
- **Later months:** opening a later month adds the transaction on the same day. A 31st series lands on Feb 28 (Feb 29 in leap years), Mar 31 and Apr 30. It stays a "31st" series even after you edit the Feb 28 copy. That case was broken at first; a logic test caught it and I fixed it.
- **No duplicates:** each series remembers which months it has already filled in. Reopening a month, going back and forth or reloading never adds a second copy. If you delete one month's copy, it doesn't come back.
- **Recurring screen:** a new tab, "Recurring (n)", lists every repeating transaction with its day, amount and start month, and whether it is still repeating or stopped. "Stop…" asks for a month, tells you which months stay unchanged, removes it from that month onward, and never adds it again.

**Choices I made that you didn't specify:**
- **Editing a copy also changes later months.** Months before it stay as they are, and the form says so.
- **A repeating copy can't be moved to another month.** You get a clear message; you can untick "Repeat monthly" first and then move it.
- **Unticking "Repeat monthly" while editing stops the series after that month.** Ticking it on a one-off transaction starts a series from that month.
- **Stopping from the first month deletes the series everywhere**, after a confirmation.
- **Only months you open get filled in.** If you jump from January to June, March gets its copy when you first open March.
- **"Export CSV" moved** from the page header into the Transactions panel, because the new tabs didn't fit at 375px. It still exports the selected month.

The new logic is in `src/lib/recurring.ts` and the new screen in `src/components/RecurringScreen.tsx`. Data saved by the earlier version loads without any loss. Nothing is committed.

**What I tested and how**
- **Logic tests** (`src/lib/recurring.test.ts`, 27 tests, `npm test`):
  - Last-day handling for 28-, 30- and 31-day months and leap years.
  - The first copy is linked to its series.
  - Later months get their copy, and jumping ahead fills only the month opened.
  - Nothing appears before the start month, reopening adds nothing, and a deleted copy stays deleted.
  - A lost record of a filled-in month can't cause a duplicate, and several series work side by side.
  - Edits change this and later months but not earlier ones, and editing the Feb 28 copy keeps the series on the 31st.
  - Moving a repeating copy to another month is refused; unticking, re-ticking and ticking a one-off all work.
  - Stopping from a middle month, a not-yet-opened month and the first month, plus the stop-month error messages.
  - Deleting a category moves its series to Other, and older saved data upgrades cleanly.
- **Browser tests** (`e2e/recurring.spec.ts`, real Chrome, at 1280px and 375px):
  - Add a Rent series on Jan 31, a Salary series and a one-off coffee.
  - Step through Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30, and Feb 29 in 2032.
  - Revisit months and reload, checking the saved transaction count doesn't change.
  - Edit February's copy: the error for moving months, the amount change carrying to March but not January.
  - Delete one month's copy and confirm it doesn't come back.
  - On the Recurring screen: the list, the stop-month error, stopping Rent from March, then checking January and February are unchanged and March, April, September and 2032 have no Rent.
  - Untick repeat while editing, tick repeat on a one-off, reload directly on the Recurring screen, and stop a series from its first month.
  - No sideways scrolling and no console errors.
- **Screenshots I looked at:**
  - The edit form, the April overview, the stop form and the list, at both sizes.
  - They led to three layout fixes: a gap above the Recurring card, a stretched month field on desktop, and the "Stop…" button wrapping on mobile.
  - After the fixes I re-ran every test and checked the screenshots again.
